loot.map_description: On the northern exit road from Watson Bay, in Grassrivers — a large fenced compound footprint.

loot.name: Crabshack Research Outpost — Crabshack VF5 (hidden discovery)
loot.area: Abandoned research outpost / boathouse in the Pelican Valley swamp

loot.name: Crabshack VF5
loot.detail: Locked in the shack at the end of the wooden walkway — door code 0212. A stash bag of marked bills sits next to it.

loot.name: Safe cash + marked bills
loot.detail: Safe code 0072, next to the PC; the safe holds cash and a note with the door code. The marked bills are turned in at Brian's drop-off after his rent job — the money arrives a day later (OutputLag).

loot.cash_estimate: Safe cash amount not published in the sources checked; plus the marked-bills payout via Brian's drop-off.

guards.description: No human guards — the hazards are environmental: a giant crab attacks at the PC (mash the prompt), and alligators patrol the swamp. Go in daylight.

loot.directions: 1) Open the map and head for the Pelican Valley swamp. The outpost is a cluster of shacks out in the swamp, so a boat or jet ski is the easy way in — go in daylight, because alligators in the swamp water can kill you fast and the outpost is hard to find your way around at night (OutputLag). 2) Land at the outpost and find the main building: switch on the electrical box at the back of it so the computer gets power. 3) Examine the floorboards — several passwords are scratched into the wood. 4) Log into the PC with the password CLEAVES (the on-screen options are shuffled, so pick whichever button shows that word). 5) Back out of the PC and a giant crab attacks — mash the on-screen button to throw it off. 6) Open the safe next to the computer with 0072; it holds cash and a note with the door code. 7) Follow the wooden walkway back to the first shack — the one with a keypad on its blood-stained wall — and enter 0212. 8) The Crabshack VF5 is just inside, next to a stash bag of marked bills. Note: the marked bills are not spendable yet — you turn them in at Brian's drop-off once you have done his rent collection job, and the money arrives a day later.
loot.map_description: An isolated boathouse/outpost in the Pelican Valley swamp — a cluster of stilt shacks over the water, reached by boat or jet ski, away from any town label. In map view there is no named marker for it: waypoint the swamp shoreline cluster in Pelican Valley and navigate the last stretch by the shacks themselves. Like other unique guns, the VF5 should show a yellow marker on your map once you are close (OutputLag).

loot.name: Pelican Valley Wrecked Cabin — two legendaries (hidden discovery)
loot.area: Wrecked cabin in the Pelican Valley swamp

loot.name: Swamp Bait Akulus
loot.detail: Lying on the bloody floor in the middle of the cabin — no fight needed to take it.

loot.name: Cruel Huntsman's SM-69
loot.detail: On the far side / back porch / wooden walkway of the cabin, with sniper ammo beside it.

loot.cash_estimate: No cash documented — the value is two legendary weapons in one trip.

guards.description: No guards documented; watch the swamp water and alligators on the approach.

loot.directions: 1) Open the map and head into the Pelican Valley swamp — the same swamp as the Crabshack research outpost, so combine both guns in one boat trip. Detonated also places this cabin as a waterfront shack in the marsh southwest of Hamlet. 2) Watch the water on the way in — the swamp is alligator country. 3) Find the wrecked cabin in the middle of the swamp: it is wrecked and covered in blood inside. 4) The Swamp Bait Akulus revolver is lying in the open on the bloody floor in the middle of the room — no fight needed, just pick it up. 5) Keep going to the far side of the cabin: the Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 hunting sniper rifle is there with sniper ammo beside it (ShowGamer places it on the wooden walkway/boardwalk outside the cabin, so check the walkway and back porch as you leave). 6) You leave with two unique guns from one stop — the revolver and the hunting sniper.
loot.map_description: A lone ruined cabin in the middle of the Pelican Valley swamp, near the Crabshack research outpost — Detonated describes the same spot as a waterfront shack in the marsh southwest of Hamlet. There is no town or business label to aim at in map view: waypoint the swamp itself in Pelican Valley, come in by water, and look for the single wrecked cabin standing in the marsh rather than a cluster of buildings.

loot.name: Conspiracist Bunker — Type 9 + rocket launcher (hidden discovery)
loot.area: Underground bunker/armory beneath a satellite-dish-covered trailer in a junk-filled trailer lot
loot.island_region: Balsero, southwest of Griffin Shooting Range (OutputLag describes the lot as in Mariana County, under the 'Leonida' lettering on the map — see notes)

loot.name: Conspiracist Type 9
loot.detail: In an open case on the workbench in the bunker. Frag grenades nearby.

loot.name: Hauners H-AT rocket launcher
loot.detail: In the corner by the safes. IMPORTANT: this is a NORMAL pickup, not a unique variant — you lose it if you die or get busted, so store it in a personal vehicle trunk.

loot.cash_estimate: No cash documented; two heavy weapons in one hidden room.

guards.description: No guards documented — a hidden, unguarded bunker.

loot.directions: 1) Open the map: OutputLag places this lot in Mariana County, just under the letters of the word 'Leonida' on the map, north of Vice City; ShowGamer and Detonated place the same trailer southwest of Griffin Shooting Range in Balsero — use both framings when you search the area (see the map note on this entry). 2) Find the junk-filled trailer lot and jump the fence. 3) Look for the one trailer covered in satellite dishes and antennas, with an old American flag on its side — that is the right trailer. 4) Go inside, open the trapdoor at the back of the trailer and climb down into the bunker. 5) The Conspiracist Type 9 sits in an open case on the workbench — its pickup prompt names it in gold, the sign of a unique gun. 6) Grab the frag grenades nearby and the rocket launcher in the corner by the safes. Important: only the Type 9 is a keepable unique — the rocket launcher is a normal pickup you lose if you die, so store it in your personal vehicle's trunk. The owner has blown himself up down there, and his phone holds the video of how.
loot.map_description: A trailer lot that reads in map view only as scattered trailers in open ground. OutputLag: a junk-filled lot in Mariana County sitting just under the 'Leonida' map lettering, north of Vice City. ShowGamer/Detonated: beneath a mobile home southwest of Griffin Shooting Range in Balsero. The two descriptions may be the same site loosely located, or two similar sites — waypoint the trailer lot nearest the dish-covered trailer landmark and confirm on foot by the satellite dishes, antennas and flag, not by the map label.

loot.name: Permit Keys Spy Vessel Wreck — Assassin Nipper.38 (hidden discovery)
loot.area: Derelict spy vessel shipwreck at the southeast edge / southern tip of the southeastern Permit Keys island, near Mile Zero Air Station

loot.name: Assassin Nipper.38
loot.detail: Behind a floor hatch inside the wreck; part of the spy-boat side puzzle. Five sources document this one (ShowGamer, TheGamesWiki, GTA6Info, Detonated, MyGamepadTester).

loot.cash_estimate: No cash documented.

guards.description: No guards documented — an offshore wreck.

loot.directions: 1) Open the map and zoom to the Permit Keys, the island chain at the far southern edge of the map, off Mile Zero Air Station. 2) Take a boat out to the southeastern Permit Keys island — the wreck is at that island's southern tip (ShowGamer), described by Detonated as a shipwreck in the SE Permit Keys near Mile Zero Air Station (the 'spy boat' puzzle). 3) Find the derelict spy vessel wreck at the island's southeast edge / southern tip and board it. 4) Inside the vessel, open the floor hatch to reach the Assassin Nipper .38. 5) Combine this with the Smuggler Gorse 425 on the neighboring island east of Mile Zero Air Station in the same boat trip, so you only make the long run south once.
loot.map_description: The southern tip of the southeastern Permit Keys island, just off Mile Zero Air Station, far south of the mainland at the bottom edge of the map. In map view, follow the Permit Keys chain to its southeastern island and drop the waypoint on that island's southernmost point — the wreck sits on/at that tip, not in the island's center. If you reach Mile Zero Air Station's label, you are in the right cluster of islands.
loot.chapter_available: Free roam; chapter not documented in sources checked

loot.name: Permit Keys Smuggler's Boat — Smuggler Gorse 425 (hidden discovery)
loot.area: Shore of a small Permit Keys island east of Mile Zero Air Station, beside an abandoned smuggler's boat

loot.name: Smuggler Gorse 425
loot.detail: Dull green finish with a moth decal. Lying by the abandoned smuggler's boat on the shore.

loot.cash_estimate: No cash documented.

guards.description: No guards documented.

loot.directions: 1) Open the map and zoom to the Permit Keys at the far southern edge of the map, around Mile Zero Air Station. 2) Boat out to the small Permit Keys island east of Mile Zero Air Station — a separate, smaller island from the southeastern one holding the spy vessel wreck. 3) Circle to the island's shore and look for the abandoned smuggler's boat washed up there (Detonated: a washed-up smuggler's boat on an island east of Mile Zero). 4) The Smuggler Gorse 425 shotgun is beside the boat on the shore — Detonated describes this variant as dull green with a moth decal, so you can confirm it on pickup. 5) Do this on the same boat trip as the Assassin Nipper .38 spy vessel at the southeastern island's southern tip, just nearby.
loot.map_description: A small island in the Permit Keys east of the Mile Zero Air Station label, at the southern edge of the map. In map view, find Mile Zero Air Station first, then move one small island east — waypoint that island's shore rather than its center, because the boat and the Gorse 425 sit washed up at the waterline, not inland.
loot.chapter_available: Free roam; chapter not documented in sources checked

loot.name: Port Vice City Scoop Containers — two legendaries (hidden discovery)
loot.area: Port Vice City cargo container area

loot.name: Mercenary LMG 6
loot.detail: Inside a yellow Scoop container at the north end of the cargo area — easiest approached from the water.

loot.name: Cargo H&L.38
loot.detail: Inside another yellow Scoop container in the cargo area — climb the container stack and break in.

loot.cash_estimate: No cash documented; two legendary weapons in one cargo yard.

guards.description: Port security in the cargo area — expect resistance when breaking into the containers (Detonated).

loot.directions: 1) Open the map and find Port Vice City (labelled 'Port Vice City' in game) — Vice City's island port district, printed on the official map on the waterfront southeast of Waxman Island and northwest of Catalan Bay. Bridges over Catalan Bay join it to Downtown on one side and Gloriana Key on the other, and the raised Mariner's Highway carries traffic in from Downtown. 2) Head into the container cargo area — the stacks of shipping containers (the island's passenger terminal is at its northwestern end, so work from there into the cargo stacks). 3) For the Mercenary LMG 6: go to the northern side of the cargo area, ideally approaching from the water side, and open the yellow Scoop container there. 4) For the Cargo H&L .38 revolver: find the other yellow Scoop container in the cargo area; the stack behind it has one container short enough to climb — get on top of that stack, then jump across to the Scoop container and break in (TheGamesWiki). Detonated notes there is security in the cargo area, so expect guards around the stacks. 5) Both unique weapons are inside yellow Scoop-branded containers — ignore the plain containers.
loot.map_description: Port Vice City is an island in map view, southeast of Waxman Island across Catalan Bay from Downtown, with its passenger terminal at the northwestern end and the container cargo area of stacked boxes as the dominant feature. Waypoint the cargo stacks, not the terminal: the LMG's yellow Scoop container is on the northern side of the cargo area by the water, and the revolver's Scoop container sits deeper in the stacks, reached by climbing the shorter stack behind it.
loot.chapter_available: Free roam; chapter not documented in sources checked

loot.name: Donnie's H&L.38 — mission trunk loot (MISSABLE)
loot.area: Trunk of Donnie's '85 Blista during the 'Don Gone' mission (Chapter 1, mission 18)

loot.name: Donnie's H&L.38
loot.detail: Unique variant in the trunk of Donnie's car. Store version sells for $1,075, but this one is free — IF you open the trunk before destroying the car. NOTE: this is the one genuinely missable entry in this file, and it is mission loot, not a free-roam stash. (The Skunk Ape questline's Mister Mangrove Laird 350 tranquilizer rifle is likewise a mission reward, not loot, and is deliberately excluded from this dataset.)

loot.cash_estimate: Weapon only; saves the $1,075 store price.

guards.description: Mission combat in Don Gone — the risk isn't guards, it's destroying the car before looting the trunk.

loot.directions: 1) This is NOT a free-roam location — it happens inside the Chapter 1 story mission Don Gone (mission 18), which comes right after Swamped (17) near the end of Chapter 1. 2) During the mission, Jason packs Donnie's things at the trailer and loads them into the trunk of Donnie's '85 Blista, then drives it off to destroy it somewhere quiet (OutputLag). 3) At that moment — when the car is stopped and before you drive it to its destruction — walk to the back of the Blista and OPEN THE TRUNK FIRST. 4) Take Donnie's H&L .38 out of the trunk (Detonated describes this variant as black with a hawk-and-flowers grip; the store version of the base revolver costs $1,075). 5) Only after the revolver is in your inventory, complete the objective that destroys the car. 6) If you wreck or burn the car first, the gun goes with it for the whole playthrough: there is no mission replay in GTA VI, and only loading an older save brings the chance back.
loot.map_description: Not a map location at all — do not go looking for a waypoint. The H&L .38 exists only inside the Don Gone mission sequence in late Chapter 1, in the trunk of Donnie's '85 Blista during the short window between loading the car at the trailer and destroying it. If you are replaying from a save, load one from before Don Gone starts; once the mission's car is destroyed, no map location will ever offer this variant again.

eggs.name: Dexter Morgan's Apartment (Trinity Apartments)
eggs.area: Trinity Apartments, Washington Island, Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County
eggs.what_it_is: Rockstar rebuilt Dexter Morgan's Miami condo block from the TV series Dexter as a visitable waterfront apartment building. The name is itself a clue: 'Trinity' nods to the Trinity Killer from Season 4, and the block copies the real Bay Harbor Islands complex used for exterior shots in the show. Dexter's unit is the second-floor corner apartment, but the door is locked, there is no interior, and Dexter never appears — the egg lives outside: a kill kit on the roof and his boat at the dock.
eggs.what_you_get: Orange toolbox on the roof with a $68 cash pickup and a knife pickup, alongside the displayed kill kit (syringe, knife, rope, tape, handcuffs). At the west dock you can steal and drive the Lure Predator L35P boat, styled after Dexter's Slice of Life.
directions: Finish the Prologue — the area is open in your first free-roam session.
Open the map and zoom into Washington Island, Vice Beach, east-northeast of Penmarch Isle.

Set your waypoint on the apartment building itself (the angular building with a pool in the middle), NOT on the 'Washington Island' text — the text drops you about a block too far east. The building sits between the Pay 'N' Spray icon and the Vice Beach Top Fun Drones icon.
Identify the light-blue, two-story block with a cylinder/spiral staircase on its south side and the Trinity symbol on the tower.
Climb the spiral staircase to the second-floor walkway, walk west to the last door — the corner unit facing the water is Dexter's (locked).
For the roof: take the metal ladder near the upper-floor hallway up to the roof and check the orange toolbox and kill-kit props.
For the boat: go back down and walk to the dock on the west side of the building; board the first boat in the row (Lure Predator L35P).
eggs.map_description: Washington Island is the small island in Vice Beach, east-northeast of Penmarch Isle. On the zoomed map the target is the angular apartment building with a swimming pool in its middle, docks on its west (left) edge and the Pay 'N' Spray icon just east (right) of it. Local reference photos saved from guide pages: ~/workspace/dexter-map/more/insider-0.jpg (county zoom), insider-1.jpg (Vice Beach zoom), insider-3.jpg (Washington Island labels), dexterdaily-map.jpg (red-arrow map), insider-2.jpg (closest map view — pool building), insider-4.jpg (front, spiral staircase), insider-5.jpg, dexterdaily-building.jpg (poolside, teal doors), shacknews-map.png.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (GameSpot, Keen Gamer, Insider Gaming, Shacknews, Dexerto and DexterDaily all place it at the same building; Jeff has also found it in-game)

eggs.name: Dexter's Kill Room (Surfside Drive Garage)
eggs.area: Surfside Drive, southwest Key Lento, near the Crastenburg Hotel, ~1 km southwest of Jason's house
eggs.what_it_is: A second Dexter egg: an ordinary beach house in Key Lento with an enterable garage fitted out as Dexter's kill room — plastic sheeting on the walls, a central metal/surgical table, knives, cleavers and a chainsaw, an M99 bottle and syringe, and bloody black trash bags. Details double as show references: two Grant 24-oz framing hammers nod to the Trinity Killer, and the chainsaw nods to Laura Moser's death.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the sight — no confirmed cash or weapon reward inside the kill room itself. (One separate guide, BoostBaseGG, lists loot elsewhere in the same house — sniper, armor, a rocket launcher in a bathtub — and warns the occupant may attack; that house-loot claim is not part of the kill-room reports and is not cross-checked here.)
directions: Travel to Key Lento in the Leonida Keys and head to the lower-middle/southwest part of the island.
Find Surfside Drive, near the Crastenburg Hotel, roughly 1 km southwest of Jason's house.
Look for a beach house with an attached garage facing the road (one guide notes a beach ball on the garage floor as a marker).
Walk up to the white garage door and use the Break In prompt to lift it.
Step inside to see the plastic-lined room: kill table on the left, chainsaw on the counter to the right, hammers, cleaver, and the M99 bottle and syringe under the table.
eggs.map_description: On the Key Lento map, aim for the southwest shore along Surfside Drive, near the Crastenburg Hotel icon, about 1 km southwest of Jason's Chapter 1 house. The target is a single house with its garage facing the street.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Dexerto, Beebom, Dot Esports and DexterDaily agree on Surfside Drive, Key Lento and the garage contents; GTA6Info's own page flags its version of this section as single-source, but the four dedicated guides above independently agree). No image URLs were extracted from those pages in this research pass, so none are listed rather than guessed.

eggs.name: The Skunk Ape (Leonida's Bigfoot) & Kirk's Questline
eggs.area: Wooded roadside southeast of Cottonmouth Lake, south of Hamlet, Mariana County (also reported around Gullet Marsh / Gambit Bay)
eggs.what_it_is: Leonida's Bigfoot: a foul-smelling ape creature you first meet in free roam standing over a deer carcass at the end of a dirt road. Shooting does not injure it in the first encounter — you follow it on foot to an effigy tree, inspect the effigy, black out, and wake up back at your vehicle. A three-mission Strangers & Freaks chain from Kirk turns the sighting into a full hunt that ends with a tranquilizer rifle and a very strange 'Mr. Mangrove.'
eggs.what_you_get: Free-roam sighting alone: nothing tangible. Questline: Mission 1 'Search for the Skunk Ape' pays $1,000; Mission 2 'Search for Tree Effigies' pays $0 but unlocks the finale; Mission 3 'Help Kirk Find Mr. Mangrove' (Chapter 2 onward, as Lucia, night only) gives the unique Mister Mangrove Laird 350 tranquilizer rifle (handed to you when you board Kirk's helicopter and kept either way) plus up to $10,000 — $5,000 if you shoot Mr. Mangrove immediately, $10,000 if you negotiate/confront Kirk first and then shoot Mr. Mangrove, $0 if you shoot Kirk or nobody. Questline total: up to $11,000 plus the rifle.
directions: Open the map and find Hamlet in Mariana County and Cottonmouth Lake just north of it; the confirmed sighting ground is the woods and mangroves south of town. GTAside places the first sighting in the mangroves around Gullet Marsh, across Gambit Bay from Jason's house in Key Lento, and other players report the creature further north in the Grassrivers and around Cottonmouth Lake, near effigies made of straw and rope.
Head to the wooded roadside southeast of Cottonmouth Lake, south of Hamlet, and follow the dirt road to its end.
Look for the creature standing over a deer carcass at the road's end, feeding on it.
Do NOT shoot it — bullets don't injure it in this encounter. Chase/follow it on foot into the trees instead (GTAside: use Focus Mode while chasing and you will lose it in the trees).

You will come across a figure tied to a tree — the tree/human effigy. Examine it and ride out the blackout; you pass out with one last look at a pair of very large feet, and wake back at your vehicle.

Quest route: flyers asking whether anyone has seen a skunk ape are posted around Leonida from Chapter 1. Read Kirk's flyer (e.g. at Skeeter's bar in Hamlet) to add Kirk to your phone contacts, then call him to start 'Search for the Skunk Ape'.
The mission only starts at night — if you arrive in daylight, advance time at home first.

Complete the effigy search mission, then wait for the Chapter 2 finale with Kirk and make your choice at the end for the payout you want. If you find a straw-and-rope effigy in the woods anywhere in this region, stay a while and listen — players report activity around them.
eggs.map_description: On the map, find Hamlet in Mariana County and Cottonmouth Lake; the sighting spot is in the woods southeast of the lake, south of the town, at the end of a dirt road near the shore facing Key Lento across Gambit Bay. GTAside's framing puts the first sighting in the Gullet Marsh mangroves across the bay from Jason's house — the two descriptions cover the same south-Hamlet shoreline woods, so waypoint the end of the dirt road on the shore southeast of the lake rather than the lake itself.
eggs.best_time: Night — the Kirk questline missions are night-only; the finale requires Lucia in Chapter 2 or later.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (GTAside, Game8, GTA6-Life, GameTrek and others agree on the Cottonmouth Lake / Hamlet area sighting and the Kirk chain; payout figures come from the earlier Keen Gamer / PowerPyx / GTA6Info / OfZen cross-check in this chat)

eggs.name: UFO Abduction near the Starlet Motel
eggs.area: Dirt road northwest of the Starlet Motel, Kelly County, east of Port Gellhorn
eggs.what_it_is: After Chapter 1, a UFO encounter can spawn on a rural road at night: an abandoned car with flashing/blinking headlights, open doors and scattered clothes points down a forest trail to a beam of light holding a woman in the air. Walk up and the craft drops her and leaves; she asks you to fetch her car, and on the way back the UFO takes YOU instead. You wake up three in-game days later, reportedly with an implant in your neck.
eggs.what_you_get: The hidden bronze trophy/achievement 'The Truth Is Out There.' No cash or item. Completing this abduction is also step 1 of the longer alien storyline (see alien-rescue-area-51). Note: Game8's Capri ritual guide also attaches this same trophy name to the demon ritual — guides disagree on which encounter grants it, or it may cover the supernatural set; the UFO attribution is the one most guides agree on.
directions: Complete Chapter 1 (the encounter needs Chapter 2 onward) and travel alone — no partner with you.
Go to the dirt road northwest of the Starlet Motel safehouse in Kelly County, east of Port Gellhorn.
Be there after 2:00 AM in-game. Look for a parked car with flashing headlights, open doors/trunk and clothes scattered nearby.
If the car isn't there, the spawn is random — drive away and come back another night.
Follow the trail in the direction the headlights point, into the woods toward the bright blue light and static sounds.
Approach the beam; the UFO drops the woman. Talk to her and offer to help.
Walk back toward her car — the UFO returns and abducts you, unlocking the trophy.
eggs.map_description: Kelly County, east of Port Gellhorn: find the Starlet Motel, then take the rural dirt road running northwest of it. The event car parks at the roadside with its headlights aimed into the trees.
eggs.best_time: After 2:00 AM, before daylight; Chapter 2 onward; solo character only.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (GameSpot, PowerPyx, Showgamer, Beebom and LibertyCity agree on place, time, solo requirement and trophy; wake-up timing is 'three days later' in most guides)

eggs.name: Alien Dreams: Rescue the Alien from the Underground Lab ('Area 51')
eggs.category: Hidden questline (sequel to the UFO abduction)
eggs.area: Starts in a dream after the UFO abduction; the real lab is at South Point Airfield, south of Hamlet, east of the Manatee Motel
eggs.what_it_is: The hidden three-part sequel to the UFO abduction. After being abducted, sleeping can trigger a strange dream: a white room on the ship, an egg room you must sneak through crouched, a solar-system room whose Earth orb reveals a real Leonida location, a keypad whose code is hidden in line markings above it, a four-button light panel, and three doors — take the milk from the left room into the machine in the right room, and never enter the middle door. The dream teaches you everything needed to break into the real restricted lab at South Point Airfield, repeat the puzzles, and carry a living alien out to its ship.
eggs.what_you_get: A permanent boost to maximum Health, Stamina and Focus after the alien is rescued and the ship collects it. No sci-fi weapon — GameRant explicitly checked and there is none. Keypad codes vary by player/playthrough (guides report 2341 and 3142 as examples) — read your own code from the markings above your keypad and reuse that same code at the real lab. The four-button panel solution is consistent across guides: 4-3-4-3-1 (buttons counted left to right).
directions: First complete the UFO abduction near the Starlet Motel (see ufo-abduction).
Play on, then sleep at a safehouse as the abducted character. The dream is random — you may need to sleep several times.
In the dream's white room, turn around and go through the black door.
Crouch and sneak along the left side of the egg room — moving fast or touching eggs restarts the section.
In the solar-system room, interact with the Earth orb and note the revealed location (South Point Airfield, south of Hamlet).
At the keypad, count the lines in the markings above it to get your four-digit code; enter it and REMEMBER it.
At the four-button panel, press 4, 3, 4, 3, 1 to light all the lights.
Of the three doors: enter the LEFT room, pick up the milk bottle, then enter the RIGHT room and put the milk in the machine. Never enter the middle door — it's a death trap. You wake up.
Travel to South Point Airfield, south of Hamlet (restricted compound east of the Manatee Motel). Ram the gate with a vehicle (or shoot the lock).
Head to the right side of the compound, break through the double doors, and go down the stairs to the keypad door.
Enter the SAME code from your dream, repeat the 4-3-4-3-1 panel and the milk/left-right door steps.
Pick up the alien from its canister — this triggers a gas release, so run to the elevator and escape. Outside, the ship collects the alien and grants the permanent stat boosts.
eggs.map_description: The real facility is the fenced, restricted compound at South Point Airfield, directly south of Hamlet in Mariana County, east of the Manatee Motel. In the dream, the Earth orb shows you this airfield location.
eggs.best_time: The chain starts with the after-2 AM UFO abduction; the dream itself triggers randomly when sleeping afterward.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Showgamer, Beebom, GameRant and Sportskeeda independently walk through the same dream, puzzles and South Point rescue; earlier list sites GTAside/GTA6Box had flagged the sequel as single-source, but four dedicated guides now corroborate it. The only variance is the keypad code, which is per-player by design)

eggs.name: The Literal Easter Egg (Nest on the Tallest Tower)
eggs.area: Top of the red-and-white radio/TV tower in Bluegrass, southern Vice-Dale County, just north of Hamlet
eggs.what_it_is: Rockstar hid an actual Easter egg: a bird's nest full of colorful painted eggs sits on the top platform of the tallest broadcast tower in the south of the map. The climb takes roughly 5–8 minutes. Pick up an egg and throw it off the edge — when it lands (in the detailed accounts, it smashes onto a vehicle/windshield below), a short secret cutscene plays.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the secret cutscene — no item, cash or trophy reported by any guide.
directions: Save your game first, and bring a parachute if you have one (Showgamer's advice) — the climb takes about seven minutes of ladders, with nothing to catch you if you slip (GTAside).
Open the map and find Hamlet in the south; the tower is in Bluegrass, southern Vice-Dale County, just north of Hamlet.

Take the highway north through Hamlet toward South Vice-Dale County and look for the massive red-and-white communications tower dominating the skyline — it is described by guides as the tallest TV/radio tower in the county.
Head to the tower's base, jump over the surrounding fence, and locate the ladder attached to the structure.
Climb all the way to the highest platform — about 5 minutes sprint-climbing, 7–8 minutes at a normal pace (Dexerto: five to eight minutes depending on speed).
At the top, look to your right for the bird's nest filled with colorful Easter eggs.
Pick up one egg and throw it over the edge of the platform, as hard/far as you can, and let it fall to the ground below.
Watch the hidden cutscene when the egg lands. You only need to throw one egg — there is no need to collect the others or repeat the process.
eggs.map_description: Southern edge of Vice-Dale County: waypoint the massive red-and-white mast just north of Hamlet in the Bluegrass area, visible from the highway running north out of town. In map view you are looking for the tower structure itself at the Hamlet end of the highway — once you can see the skyline, the tower dominates it, so the last stretch is navigated by sight rather than by the map.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Dexerto, Showgamer, GameRant, Game8, Sportskeeda, ComicBook, Games.gg, GTAside and GTA6Info all agree: south Vice-Dale tower north of Hamlet, nest on the top platform, throw an egg for the cutscene)

eggs.name: The Belville 'Simulation' House (from the 2021 San Andreas Photo)
eggs.area: Belville, Leonard County
eggs.what_it_is: In 2021, a photo inside the Lil' Probe'Inn in GTA: San Andreas — The Definitive Edition showed a house players assumed was a GTA VI tease. On launch day a mapping-community member found the identical house — pale yellow, double garage, two palm trees, same vegetation — in Belville, Leonard County. Force the garage and you find the home of a conspiracy theorist who has figured out he lives in a video game: his notes cover NPCs who are identical, doors that aren't real, buildings you can't enter, man-made storms, and his failed attempts to leave the state.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the sight — reading the notes/boards in the garage. Two extra claims appear in only one or two newer write-ups and are NOT cross-checked: a meteorite under the bed sellable on LifeInvader (LibertyCity) and an Illuminaughty card on the pinboard (CutsSceneWire). Treat those as unconfirmed extras, not rewards.
directions: Travel to Belville in Leonard County.
Look for a pale yellow single-storey house with a double garage, two palm trees in front, and an estate-agent sign reading roughly 'You've got the dream job. Now get the dream house.'
Crouch at the bottom of the garage door — a prompt appears to force it open.

Go inside and read the main board ('I can't take it anymore') and the notes around the garage: 'The doors aren't real,' 'Storms are man made,' the violent-crime graph, and his escape plans (plane ticket to Los Santos, driving past the state line, a boat).
Note the recurring 'six' references and that 'J and L' are marked as immune to whatever he's describing.
eggs.map_description: Belville, Leonard County: a single pale-yellow house with a double garage and two palms, matching the 2021 photo almost exactly. It has no map marker — the garage, palms and estate-agent sign are the identifiers.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified for the house, garage break-in and simulation notes (Dexerto, GTABites, GTAside, plus CutsSceneWire/SlateSource coverage). The meteorite and Illuminaughty-card extras are single-source and flagged as such in what_you_get.

eggs.name: The Talking Parrot & the Exotic Animal Front (Strange Noises)
eggs.area: Three Sheets Liquor, Key Lento (next to the Pay 'N' Spray); starts at Shirley's house east of Jason's house
eggs.what_it_is: A hidden cash stash guarded by a talking parrot, tied to the 'Strange Noises' activity. Shirley asks you to fetch her some rum from Three Sheets Liquor; players who ask the cashier about the strange bird noises get pointed out back, where criminals are running an exotic-animal front behind the store. Clear them out and the red parrot in the middle cage will, if asked twice, say one word: 'generator' — the stash is hidden in a vent right beside it.
eggs.what_you_get: Cash in the small air vent next to the generator behind the parrot: guides report $1,200–$1,382 for the vent stash itself (Polygon says the haul is over $1,000; DualShockers gives $1,382; Showgamer $1,361; Insider Gaming ~$1,200). More loot (including a back-room safe and weapons like machetes) can push the total higher in some accounts (~$2,500 per Insider Gaming), but totals vary by source — the vent stash figure is the consistent one. Deposit the cash in BuckMe afterward.
directions: Availability: Chapter 1, once you've reached the Pipework area. This activity is missable — do it before the Tourist Trap point of no return.
Find Shirley at her house east of Jason's house on Peach Palm Drive (corner house, white fence, striped umbrella) and take her rum errand.
Go to Three Sheets Liquor, south of Jason's safehouse off Sunbelt Highway, north of the Pay 'N' Spray and south of the Flip Flop House.
Inside, ask the cashier about the bird noises.
Exit and take the path between the liquor store and the Pay 'N' Spray; hop the wall/opening into the back yard.
Clear out the criminals in the yard — be ready for a fight.
Find the red parrot in the middle cage and interact with it TWICE; it will say 'generator.'
Go to the generator in the corner behind the parrot and check the small air vent right next to it for the cash (Focus mode highlights the crevice in DualShockers' account).
Police arrive soon after the last criminal dies — flee south, hopping fences, and deposit the money.
eggs.map_description: Key Lento: Three Sheets Liquor sits just north of the Pay 'N' Spray on the Sunbelt Highway side, south of Jason's safehouse. The animal yard is directly behind the store, reached by the gap between the store and the Pay 'N' Spray.
eggs.best_time: Chapter 1 — missable after Tourist Trap locks the story.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Polygon, DualShockers, Showgamer, Insider Gaming and GTAside agree on Three Sheets, the parrot, 'generator' and the vent stash). Cash amounts differ slightly between guides ($1,200–$1,382), so a range is given rather than one absolute figure.

eggs.name: The Giant Crab & the Pelican Valley Outpost Puzzle
eggs.category: Creature encounter / multi-step puzzle with loot
eggs.area: Pelican Valley Outpost, Gullet Marsh (Grassrivers / Mariana County swamps, just north of the Leonida Keys)
eggs.what_it_is: An abandoned research outpost in the swamp hides a chained puzzle — and a person-sized mutant crab that drops on you mid-investigation, a nod to the 2006 'giant enemy crab' meme. The outpost (a stilt house, a lab shed, a big blue pool and a pier with a locked boathouse) is wired with codes hidden in its own paperwork: a floorboard password, a lab specimen number, and an 'Emergency Go Protocol' that unlocks the final room and a unique SMG.
eggs.what_you_get: Safe (code 0072): a little over $1,000 (Cut.pro says ~$1,070) plus the note revealing protocol 0212. Boathouse (code 0212): the unique Crabshack VF5 SMG (called 'Crabshack SMG' in one guide) next to a corpse. Cut.pro's combined walkthrough also reports a bag with $10,000 in the boathouse — that $10,000 bag is reported by fewer sources than the SMG and is flagged here as less certain.
directions: Find the Pelican Valley Outpost in Gullet Marsh: a wooden building on stilts with a smaller lab building beside it, a big blue pool, and a pier ending in a locked boathouse.
Turn the power ON at the breaker box outside (right side of the house, near white containers and a green hose in PlayDay's account).
Go inside and check the bedroom floorboards for the computer password: CLEAVES.
Use the computer in the office (left of the front door) with password CLEAVES and read the diary/journal.
Step away from the computer — the giant crab drops from the ceiling. Fight it off.
In the lab, read the clipboard for specimen 0036, marked 'success.'
The safe clue is 'double the success': 0036 doubled = 0072. Open the safe with 0072 and take the cash and the note ('Emergency Go Protocol 0212').
Go to the boathouse at the end of the pier and enter 0212.
Inside, take the Crabshack VF5 next to the corpse (and check for the cash bag reported by Cut.pro).
eggs.map_description: Gullet Marsh swampland in the Grassrivers/Pelican Valley area, southwest Leonida just north of the Leonida Keys: look for an isolated outpost on the water — stilt house plus lab shed, blue pool, and a pier running out to a boathouse. Region naming varies between guides (Gullet Marsh / Grassrivers / Pelican Valley) but all describe the same outpost layout.
eggs.confidence: medium-high — the encounter and the full puzzle chain (breaker → CLEAVES → journal → crab → 0036 → safe 0072 → boathouse 0212 → Crabshack VF5) are corroborated by GamerHour, Cut.pro, PlayDay and GTAside. The $10,000 boathouse bag rests on fewer sources.

eggs.name: The Jet-Ski Rescue Dog & Dog Island (Cool Dog / Lucky Dog)
eggs.area: Open water — easiest in Gambit Bay, west of Key Lento (also reported in the Gulf of Leonida and Partridge Bay, Lummox County)
eggs.what_it_is: Strand yourself in open water and help arrives: a German shepherd in an orange life vest and goggles rides up on a jet ski, barking. The game prompts name him Cool Dog (the community also calls him Lucky Dog); GameSpot reports he is seemingly based on a real viral Florida jet-ski dog, though Rockstar has not confirmed that. Ride with him past the first beach and he takes you to a secret island full of dogs, where playing with them pays off.
eggs.what_you_get: On Dog Island, play fetch / praise / pet the dogs until one digs up a wallet with $1,218 (OfZen and Showgamer give the exact figure; Beebom and GTAside round it to ~$1,200). Showgamer additionally reports free sports sunglasses in a container near the overturned boat/canoe shelter on the island — that extra is reported by fewer sources.
directions: Take a boat out into open water — Gambit Bay west of Key Lento is the most reliable spot.
Leave the boat and swim away from it, out to sea, for roughly 5 minutes. Stay far from land, other boats and islands — being near any of them stops the trigger.
Listen for barking: the dog arrives on a jet ski wearing a life vest and goggles.
Hold L2/LT to interact; use Praise, then choose Ride when the prompt appears.
Stay on the jet ski PAST the first beach he passes — riding on is what reaches Dog Island.
On the island, play fetch, praise and pet the dogs until one digs up the wallet with $1,218.
Note: the island can't be waypointed and its drop-off spot appears randomly — don't count on returning the same way.
eggs.map_description: No fixed map point: the trigger is open water. Gambit Bay, the bay west of Key Lento in the Leonida Keys, is the most-cited launch area; swim west out to sea from there. Dog Island itself is unmarked and not reliably re-findable.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (OfZen, Beebom, Showgamer, GameSpot, GamesHorizon and GTAside agree on the stranded-swim trigger, the dog's outfit, Dog Island and the ~$1,200 wallet). The real-life-dog inspiration is reported as 'seemingly based on,' not confirmed by Rockstar.

eggs.name: Paul Walker's Fast & Furious Eclipse (Maibatsu Penumbra FF)
eggs.area: Villa garage, central Vespucci Island (Neptune Circle), Rialto Islands, Vice-Dale County
eggs.what_it_is: Brian O'Conner's lime-green 1995 Mitsubishi Eclipse from The Fast and the Furious, recreated in-game as a '97 Maibatsu Penumbra FF with the movie livery — black hood with white graphics, blue-and-white side vinyls, big rear wing, roof scoop, green underglow — and a license plate reading 'HAD YOU,' Brian's line to Dom. It's a stealable, keepable car hidden in a hedged villa garage in the middle of Vespucci Island.
eggs.what_you_get: The car itself. Take it in your first hour of free roam with no mission required. To keep it permanently, register it: Polygon lists registration at $6,750 and resale at $1,100; Keen Gamer recommends waiting until Chapter 2 and bringing it to Moses during 'Moses (Take A Vehicle to Moses)' so your first registration is free. Whether the car can be kept at all was disputed in early list coverage, but the dedicated guides above agree registration makes it permanent — an unregistered car can despawn.
directions: Cross to Vespucci Island, the oblong island in the Rialto Islands chain between Vice City and Vice Beach.

Head to the central residential streets (Neptune Circle) and find the modern villa with tall hedges and a white garage door/gate — it's across from a house under construction with a black sign, next to a white house with a big blue umbrella on its roof terrace.
The white gate opens automatically at the main entrance in Polygon's account; there are no guards.
Go to the side door beside the garage and force/break it open (this can set off the alarm — several guides say to disable the alarm panel on the wall inside).
Inside the garage is the green Penumbra FF. Before driving off, open the trunk if you want the second egg (see snake-in-the-trunk).
Smash the driver-side window (or use a slim jim if you've met Moses in Chapter 2) and hotwire it with the left/right stick prompts.
Drive out, then register the car to keep it (free as your first registration via Moses in Chapter 2, or pay the registration fee).
eggs.map_description: Vespucci Island is the middle, oblong island of the Rialto Islands in the bay between Vice City (west) and Vice Beach (east). The villa is near the island's center on Neptune Circle: tall hedge, white garage, construction site directly across the street.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Polygon, Keen Gamer, Insider Gaming, Showgamer, FandomWire, Jalopnik, SlashGear, HotCars and Game8 all place the same car in the same Vespucci Island villa garage)

eggs.name: Snake in the Trunk (Toy Story Nod)
eggs.area: Trunk of the Eclipse/Penumbra FF, villa garage, central Vespucci Island
eggs.what_it_is: A second movie joke hidden inside the first: open the trunk ('boot' in British English) of Paul Walker's Eclipse before driving away and a large snake springs out and attacks you. Players and guides read it as Woody's Toy Story catchphrase made literal — 'There's a snake in my boot.' It does no lasting harm; it's a scare, not a fight.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the sight (and the scare). No loot is in the trunk.
directions: Go to the Vespucci Island villa garage and get into the garage with the green Penumbra FF (see fast-furious-eclipse for the break-in steps).
Before getting in the car, walk to the back and interact with / break into the trunk.
The snake lunges out — that's the whole egg. Then hotwire the car and leave as normal.
eggs.map_description: Same location as the Eclipse: the hedged villa near the center of Vespucci Island, Rialto Islands. No separate map point.
eggs.confidence: medium-high — multi-source for the Eclipse-trunk placement (Insider Gaming, Showgamer, FandomWire, GTA6Locations and ViceCityHustle all describe the snake in this car's trunk, filmed by multiple launch walkthroughs). One earlier list (Astroworld) instead placed a snake-in-trunk at an old house in Leonard County and GTA6Box initially filed it as unconfirmed — that alternate placement is not corroborated by the dedicated guides, so the Eclipse trunk is the version recorded here.

eggs.name: The Capri Pentagram Ritual (Sacrificial Demon)
eggs.area: Abandoned warehouse in northern Capri, west of Tortoise Lake, beside/west of Top Fun Drones
eggs.what_it_is: A horror set-piece hidden in an unmarked warehouse: a blood pentagram with a human-shaped outline, candles and an occult altar (whose book hints that cleansing fire is the answer). Bring an unconscious NPC and lay them on the outline and the ritual fires — lights out, candles lit, your partner screaming from a boarded room upstairs, character-specific hallucinations, and finally the sacrificed NPC reanimates as a demon that bullets and explosives cannot kill. Only fire works.
eggs.what_you_get: The full horror sequence and escape. Game8 links completing it (burning the demon) to the hidden bronze trophy 'The Truth Is Out There' — but most UFO guides attach that same trophy to the UFO abduction (see ufo-abduction), so which encounter grants it is disputed between guides. No cash or item reward is reported.
directions: Open the map and go to Capri, on the western side of Leonida: find Tortoise Lake in the north of town — the warehouse cluster sits on the west/left side of the lake, and the Grand Turkey of Capri sculpture and the Top Fun Drones business are your landmarks.

Travel to Capri and find the abandoned warehouse in the north of town — west of Tortoise Lake, just north of the Grand Turkey of Capri sculpture, beside Top Fun Drones (Game8 says beside it; Showgamer/GameRant say west of it / the south building of the cluster left of the lake).

Before starting: read the altar book's fire hint, and note your fire supplies — a gasoline can near the altar, Molotovs in the back-right corner of the ritual room, and another Molotov in a drawer upstairs. Spreading gasoline around the pentagram first makes the fight much easier.
Go outside to the nearby construction site and knock out a lone NPC (knocking out NPCs here doesn't hurt your criminal record, per Game8).
Carry the unconscious NPC inside and drop them exactly on the human-shaped outline in the center of the pentagram.

The lights cut and the candles ignite. Follow your partner's voice upstairs (flashlight helps) and check the boarded-up room — expect a hallucination sequence (as Jason: Lucia tied up, then Cal; as Lucia: Jason tied up, then her mother).
Grab the Molotov from the upstairs drawer before heading back down.
Downstairs the sacrificed NPC reanimates as the demon. Guns and explosives won't kill it — lure it onto the gasoline/pentagram and burn it with a Molotov or the gas can.
Once it's burned, leave the warehouse to end the encounter. Save before starting, and go at night for the full effect.
eggs.map_description: Capri, western Leonida: the warehouse is the southern building of the small cluster on the west/left side of Tortoise Lake in northern Capri, next to the Top Fun Drones business and just north of the Grand Turkey of Capri sculpture. The warehouse is unmarked on the map — waypoint the west shore of Tortoise Lake and use the lake, the drone shop and the turkey sculpture to orient the final approach.
eggs.best_time: Night recommended (atmosphere); no guide lists a hard time gate.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Sportskeeda, Game8, Showgamer, GameRant, GamesHorizon and GTAside agree on the warehouse, the NPC-sacrifice trigger, the upstairs sequence and the fire-only kill). Only the trophy attribution conflicts with the UFO guides.

eggs.name: SOS Island & the Found-Footage Phone
eggs.area: Tiny island in Leonida Bay / Gulf of Leonida — far west of Watson Bay and the Grassrivers, on the far-left (west) side of Mariana County, just north/above the military air base (Mile Zero Air Station)
eggs.what_it_is: A tiny palm island with two messages spelled out in trash and debris on the sand: 'SOS' and '#sendbeer' (or 'Send Beer'). Near the first S lies a dropped mobile phone; pick it up and it plays a found-footage clip of two content creators showing off 'their' private island — until something in the water attacks and the recording cuts out. No guide has found any follow-up clue on the island: it's an open mystery, framed by LeonidaNow as an unsolved case.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the sight and the phone video — no loot or reward has been found on the island.
directions: Get a boat (you'll be crossing open water).
Head to the far west of the map: out into Leonida Bay off Mariana County, north of the military air base / Mile Zero Air Station, far west of Watson Bay and the Grassrivers wetlands.
Look for a very small island with just a few palm trees and beach it.
Walk the sand to find 'SOS' spelled in trash/debris and the '#sendbeer' message nearby.
Search by the first letter S of the SOS for the mobile phone on the ground.
Interact with the phone and choose View Media to watch the video.
Optional tie-in: swimming out from this island into open water is also a way players trigger the jet-ski dog rescue (see jetski-dog-dog-island).
eggs.map_description: Guides agree on the shape of the location but phrase it differently: Showgamer/Sportskeeda say far west of Watson Bay/Grassrivers in the Gulf of Leonida; ProdigyGamers/LeonidaNow say a tiny palm island in Leonida Bay on the far-left side of Mariana County, directly above/north of the military air base. Both descriptions point to the same far-western offshore islet — use the air base as your southern landmark and scan north of it.
eggs.confidence: medium-high — multi-source verified for the island, the SOS/#sendbeer messages and the phone video (Showgamer, Sportskeeda, ProdigyGamers, GamesHorizon, QuoraMarketing and LeonidaNow). The exact placement is described two ways (west of Grassrivers vs north of the air base), so map_description gives both frames instead of one false-precise point. What attacked the creators is unexplained in every source.

eggs.name: Monument of Leonidan Supremacy (The Beeping Statue Mystery)
eggs.area: Western Manifest Canyon, Kelly County, near SR-73, north of Port Gellhorn
eggs.what_it_is: A roadside monument built (in lore) in 1982: a pillar holding up a (broken) globe, ringed by four stallion statues whose plaque says they stand for the cardinal components of Leonidan culture — wildlife, corruption, humanity and yeyo — under the slogan 'Just as America leads the world, so too does Leonida lead America.' Each horse carries different symbols on its pedestal and head, and one wears a traffic cone. The finder (Reddit user u/akspree, on launch day) reported the controller vibrating and the statue beeping in a pattern players think could be Morse code. Nobody has decoded or solved it, and Rockstar has said nothing — it's already being compared to GTA V's Mount Chiliad mystery. It is also a scannable landmark: sculpture #23 in the WAiNK sculpture set.
eggs.what_you_get: A WAiNK sculpture scan (the monument counts toward the 100 WAiNK scans / 100% completion, per the sculpture guides). The beeping/vibration mystery itself has no known reward — it is unsolved and may be a joke.
directions: Open the map and head into Kelly County, north of Port Gellhorn, toward Manifest Canyon.
Take SR-73 into western Manifest Canyon and look for the raised plaza just off the main road.
Walk up to the monument: a central pillar holding up a globe, circled by four stallions around the base.

Read the plaque (placard): it is dedicated to 'Leonidan Supremacy', built in 1982, and quotes 'Just as America leads the world, so too does Leonida lead America.' The pillar and globe stand for 'inevitable worldwide Leonidafication'.

Check each horse in turn: the placard says the four stallions stand for the cardinal components of Leonidan culture — wildlife, corruption, humanity and yeyo — and each carries different symbols on its pedestal/podium and on its head. One stallion wears a traffic cone.
Scan the monolith with your phone for the WAiNK sculpture collectible.

With controller vibration on, stand close and listen — per the original report (u/akspree, posted on launch day, November 19, 2026), the statue beeps and the pad vibrates. Record the beeps if you want to try decoding them; no solution exists yet, and the beeping/vibration rests on that one player's report.
eggs.map_description: Kelly County, western Manifest Canyon near SR-73, north of Port Gellhorn: the sculpture guides (IGN, TheGamesWiki, GTA6GPS) all pin it the same way — a monolith holding up the earth, surrounded by horse statues, on a raised plaza just off the main road through the canyon. Waypoint the plaza beside SR-73 in the western canyon rather than the canyon label itself; the pillar-and-globe silhouette is what you are scanning for as you arrive.
eggs.confidence: medium — the monument's existence, location, plaque text and sculpture-collectible status are multi-source verified (IGN, TheGamesWiki, GTA6GPS, PowerPyx via O Santuário Geek). The vibration/beeping behavior rests on ONE player's report (u/akspree) repeated by TheGamer/VGTimes and others — that behavior is single-source and the 'Morse code' reading is theory only. GTA6Box deliberately left this out of its verified list for that reason.

eggs.name: Red Hulk: Kyle McKittrick's Giant Strawberry Disaster
eggs.area: McKittrick Farm, Frogswater, Kelly County — northeast of the Starlet Motel, east of Port Gellhorn
eggs.what_it_is: Farmer Kyle McKittrick is experimenting with chemicals to grow oversized strawberries. Across a three-mission Strangers & Freaks strand — crop-dusting his fields, fetching more chemicals, then checking on him after his messages stop making sense — Kyle eats his own product and mutates into a massive red-skinned brute who tears through police, vehicles and a helicopter: Leonida's own Red Hulk, with no official Marvel connection (Rockstar has not named the creature or confirmed the reference). The finale forces a permanent choice: help the agents kill him, or let him rampage free — you can even hug him if you spare him and have the health for it.
eggs.what_you_get: Mission 1 pays $400 for the crop-dusting job. The finale pays $5,000 (paid via BuckMe by the Mutandis agent) ONLY if you help kill Kyle; sparing him pays nothing but gives the fuller ending (including the optional hug) and a later sighting of Kyle destroying the Farm Fix Meth Lab in Leonard County, north of Belville. There is no mission replay — the choice is permanent on that save.
directions: In Chapter 2, go to the Starlet Motel in Kelly County and read the 'Pilot Wanted' flyer outside the reception office.
Follow the marker to the airstrip east of the motel; Kyle lands in his crop duster. Accept the job — 'Check Out McKittrick Farm.'
Fly the crop duster: select Spray Chemicals (L1/LB weapon wheel), spray the marked field (R1/RB), land back at the airstrip, and collect $400 plus Kyle's contact.

About one in-game day later Kyle texts about 'Collect Chemicals for Kyle': retrieve the chemical shipment in Leonard County — pay the Final Chapter bikers $5,000 or steal their van — and deliver it to the farm.
Progress to Chapter 3 and wait for Kyle's garbled text (it can take several in-game days), unlocking 'Buddy? (Check on Kyle).'
Return to McKittrick Farm: police and hazmat crews surround the barn. Optionally offer the supervisor help and enter via the red door at the back of the barn.
Watch the cutscene — Kyle has mutated. Then choose: shoot Kyle with the agents for the $5,000, or stay out of it and let him escape (approach afterward for the hug if you spared him).
eggs.map_description: McKittrick Farm sits in Frogswater, Kelly County, northeast of the Starlet Motel and east of Port Gellhorn — the same motel area as the UFO encounter. The strand starts at the motel's reception flyer, not at the farm itself.
eggs.best_time: Starts in Chapter 2 (Starlet Motel flyer); finale requires Chapter 3.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Dexerto, Showgamer, Beebom, HoldToReset and TheGameExtras agree on the farm, the three missions, the transformation and the kill/spare $5,000 choice). Earlier list coverage (GTA6Box) rated this lower and GTAside filed it as unconfirmed; the dedicated mission guides supersede that.

eggs.name: Jason's Boat with a Los Santos GPS (Fan-Called 'Michael's Boat')
eggs.area: Jason's house, Key Lento, Leonida Keys — Chapter 1 only
eggs.what_it_is: Parked at Jason's Chapter 1 house is a white-and-blue Marquis sailboat, the same model as Michael De Santa's yacht that was stolen in GTA V's 'Father/Son' mission and never recovered. Climb aboard and zoom in on the dashboard GPS with binoculars: the screen shows southern Los Santos — the Port of Los Santos and the docks — instead of Leonida, which fans read as the boat's last saved position from when Michael owned it. Important honesty note: nothing in the game names the boat as Michael's, and Rockstar has not confirmed the connection — the GPS detail is verified, the ownership is fan interpretation. Michael's voice actor Ned Luke even joked about it on X ('I'm coming Jason… for my boat'), per Keen Gamer.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the sight — a close-up photo opportunity. Time-sensitive: Jason's house is destroyed in the Chapter 1 finale mission 'Home Sweet Home,' so look during Chapter 1.
directions: During Chapter 1 only, open the map and go to Jason's house in Key Lento, in the Leonida Keys — his Chapter 1 safehouse.

Find the Marquis sailboat parked beside the stilt house — NOT the fishing boat tied to the dock behind the house, which is a different vessel. GTAside describes it as a boat moored near Jason's house that looks like the yacht stolen from Michael De Santa in GTA V.
Climb aboard and go to the steering console / control panel (the navigation screen).
Aim your binoculars (or zoom) at the GPS/navigation screen.
Read the map on the screen: southern Los Santos with the port and docks — GTA V's map, not Leonida's. That screen is the whole easter egg, so get close enough to read it.
eggs.map_description: Jason's Chapter 1 safehouse in Key Lento, in the Leonida Keys — waypoint the house itself. The boat sits in the yard/dock area beside the stilt house from the moment the game begins; in map view there is no separate boat marker, so navigate to the house and then check the vessel parked beside it, not the fishing boat at the dock behind it.
eggs.best_time: Chapter 1 only — the house (and access to the boat) is lost after 'Home Sweet Home.'
eggs.confidence: medium-high — the boat and its Los Santos GPS are multi-source verified (Keen Gamer, Game8, Cut.pro, GameRant, GTAside, DamnModz; find originally by Reddit user u/rahiou, published by Output Lag on launch day). Confidence is NOT high on the claim 'this is Michael's actual boat' — that part is unconfirmed by Rockstar and unstated in-game, and the entry is worded accordingly.

eggs.name: The Ocean View Hotel Returns (Tommy Vercetti's First Safehouse)
eggs.area: Shore Drive, Ocean Beach, southern Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County
eggs.what_it_is: The Ocean View Hotel — Tommy Vercetti's first safehouse in GTA: Vice City (2002) — is back on the beachfront strip, rebuilt in modern Vice City with its Art Deco frontage (the original was partly inspired by Miami's Clevelander hotel). GTA6Info's Ocean Beach page reports players getting the 'In the Beginning…' trophy at its rooftop bar, a direct echo of the 2002 game's opening. Whether it works as a safehouse this time has not been confirmed. Separately, Rockstar's own Ultimate Edition text names the 'Vercetti Estate' as the source of the Hawk & Little Morgan revolvers — but that is edition copy, not a visitable Tommy appearance, and no source confirms Tommy himself appears.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the sight / nostalgia stop, plus (per GTA6Info) the 'In the Beginning…' trophy reported at the rooftop bar. No confirmed safehouse function or loot.
directions: Open the map and travel to Ocean Beach, the southern end of Vice Beach in Vice-Dale County — Washington Beach is to the north and South Ocean Beach is the neighboring area.
Walk or drive Shore Drive, the main beachfront strip lined with hotels, bars and cafes, with the beach boardwalk, sand and lifeguard towers directly across the street.

Find the Ocean View Hotel in the middle of the hotel row — near the Paramour Hotel and Hotel Dixon in GTADB's building-by-building matching. It is Tommy Vercetti's first safehouse from the 2002 Vice City, back again on the same strip.
Use the neon sign and the official screenshot framing (Jason and Lucia under the sign) to confirm you have the right building among the pastel Art Deco hotels.

Go up to the rooftop bar if accessible: players report getting the 'In the Beginning…' trophy there (GTA6Info describes it as a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach), and it is the photo opportunity under the neon sign.
eggs.map_description: Southern tip of the Vice Beach barrier island: Ocean Beach faces Downtown Vice City across Catalan Bay. In map view, follow Shore Drive's hotel row along the beachfront — the Ocean View sits mid-row among the pastel Art Deco hotels, with the beach directly across the street. Waypoint the middle of the Shore Drive strip in Ocean Beach rather than the Ocean Beach label, then pick out the building by its neon sign.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified that the Ocean View Hotel returns on Shore Drive, Ocean Beach (interactive map/GTADB, EarlyGame, GTAVibes, FandomWire, Showgamer, GTA6Info, plus Rockstar's own material). The rooftop-trophy detail is from GTA6Info's Ocean Beach page; safehouse function is unconfirmed in all sources.

eggs.name: Michael's 'Wind Chimes' Ringtone
eggs.area: Anywhere — your in-game phone settings
eggs.what_it_is: A tiny GTA V callback hiding in your phone: among the selectable ringtones is one called 'Wind Chimes' — the ringtone Michael De Santa used in GTA V. You can set it as your own ringtone for Jason or Lucia.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the nod — Michael's ringtone on your phone.
directions: Open your in-game phone — this works anywhere, at any time; there is no location to travel to.
Go to Settings, then Ringtones.
Select 'Windchimes' / 'Wind Chimes' from the list.
That's it — the nod is the setting itself: GTAside notes this is the ringtone Michael used in GTA V, and you can set it as your own.
eggs.map_description: No map location — available anywhere, any time, from the phone menu. There is nothing to waypoint and no building to find; the sources describe a phone setting only.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (GTAside, GameTrek and LibertyCity all describe the same ringtone setting) Directions for this entry are necessarily short: its sources describe a phone setting only — there is no location, building or map point to navigate to, so there is no further navigational detail to add.

eggs.name: 'Lethal by Design: A Liberty City Memoir' (GTA IV Book)
eggs.area: Jason's house, Key Lento — small table by the back door; Chapter 1 only
eggs.what_it_is: A readable book in Jason's house: a memoir by Tom Everett, a former Liberty City mobster, covering his life from 2006 to 2008 — GTA IV's year. LibertyCity's detailed account says Everett was meant to be one of Gracie Ancelotti's six bodyguards and missed the day the other five were killed, tying the book directly into GTA IV's kidnapping storyline with Niko Bellic and Packie McReary. It's a missable collectible read: the books in Jason's house can't be collected after Chapter 1.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the read — a short in-game book with direct GTA IV story connections. Missable: read it before the end of Chapter 1.
directions: During Chapter 1 only, open the map and go to Jason's house in Key Lento, in the Leonida Keys — his Chapter 1 safehouse.
Go inside the house and find the small table near the back door.
Pick up / interact with the book on that table: 'Lethal by Design: A Liberty City Memoir' — the GTA IV / Liberty City nod (GTAside lists it among the books lying in Jason's house).

Read it now, while you are here: Jason's house is destroyed in 'Home Sweet Home', and the house books (this one and 'Orca') can't be collected afterward, so this copy is gone for the rest of the playthrough once Chapter 1 ends.
eggs.map_description: Inside Jason's Chapter 1 safehouse in Key Lento, Leonida Keys — waypoint the house; the book itself is an interior object with no map marker, on the small table by the back door. Because the house is destroyed later in Chapter 1, the map view that matters is simply Jason's house while it still stands.
eggs.best_time: Chapter 1 only — missable after 'Home Sweet Home.'
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (GTAside, LibertyCity, GTA6Info and GameTrek agree on the book, its location by the back door, and its 2008/GTA IV subject; LibertyCity supplies the detailed Everett/Gracie connection)

eggs.name: Mount Chiliad Bar Talk (Jetpack Bunker Gossip)
eggs.area: Bar next to the meeting spot in an early story mission (Donnie / Brian meeting)
eggs.what_it_is: Early in the story, Donnie Carter calls Jason to meet him and Brian Heder and sends him to a nearby bar. Approach slowly and two NPC patrons are gossiping about Mount Chiliad in San Andreas — the craziness on the mountain and a hidden bunker underneath it with jetpacks and eggs — a straight retelling of GTA V's famous mural mystery (and, as one player quoted in coverage joked, it implies GTA Online's Doomsday Heist is canon). It's heard, not visited: there is no Chiliad location to go to in Leonida.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the overheard conversation. GamingBible notes it is ambient chatter and could not confirm every player hears it — walk in slowly and listen rather than rushing the objective.
directions: Play the early story mission where Donnie calls Jason to meet him and Brian — GTAside frames it as the early mission where Jason goes to meet Donnie and Brian at a bar.
When Donnie sends you to the bar next door, approach slowly on foot rather than rushing the objective marker.
Stop near the two patrons: GTAside places the two customers sitting outside the bar; other sources place them at a table inside — check both spots as you arrive.

Listen to the full conversation before moving on with the objective: the two customers are talking about Mount Chiliad in Blaine County, and about a hidden bunker with jetpacks and eggs under the mountain — GTA V's mural mystery retold as bar gossip.
Let the conversation finish on its own; pushing ahead with the mission objective can cut it off.
eggs.map_description: Not a free-roam map point — the bar beside the Donnie/Brian meeting spot in that early mission, so there is nothing to waypoint in free roam. The patrons' exact spot is reported inconsistently (GTAside: sitting outside the bar; others: at a table inside), so check both as you arrive during the mission.
eggs.best_time: During that early story mission only — it's missable ambient dialogue.
eggs.confidence: medium-high — multi-source verified (OutputLag, BuzzFeed, GamingBible and GTA6Box all report the same conversation, originally heard by Reddit user Tr1angleChoke and confirmed by a second player, SprungVenus). Confidence is capped because it's ambient dialogue that may not trigger for every player, and sources disagree on the patrons' exact position.

eggs.name: 'The Cowboy's Prayer Is to Die Young' (Red Dead Novel)
eggs.area: Brian's Marina office, Key Lento (Chapter 1 missions); another copy on the bar at Jacob's Tavern, Millport; a further copy in West Kalaga (Taco Bomb, per SlateSource)
eggs.what_it_is: A readable Western novel by Elijah G. Rubens following gunslinger Rust McCreary — and it retells Red Dead Redemption 2 from the sidelines: McCreary reaches the Cairn Lake cabin in Ambarino and finds Flaco Hernández dead in the snow with a forehead bullet wound, exactly as Arthur Morgan left him in RDR2's 'The Noblest of Men, and a Woman.' The book name-checks New Austin, Blackwater, Armadillo, Ambarino and Chuparosa. GameSpot separately photographed a Western about a New Austin cowboy at Jacob's Tavern in Millport on November 18, 2026.
eggs.what_you_get: Just the read — the strongest of GTA VI's several Red Dead nods. The Brian's Marina copy is available during the early Chapter 1 missions there.
directions: Earliest copy: during Chapter 1, open the map and go to Brian's Marina in Key Lento (Leonida Keys), then enter Brian Heder's office — Beebom notes this is where you start the earlier Chapter 1 missions.

Interact with the readable Western novel in the office: 'The Cowboy's Prayer Is to Die Young' by Elijah G. Rubens. It follows a character named Rust McCreary and contains the Red Dead references — Flaco Hernández, and Cairn Lake in Ambarino, plus mentions of New Austin, Blackwater, Armadillo and Chuparosa.
Alternative copy: walk into Jacob's Tavern in Millport and look for the paperback Western on the bar (GameSpot photographed this copy via GTA6Info).
A third copy is reported inside the Taco Bomb in West Kalaga (SlateSource / RetroBroker).
Interact to open and read the passages about Cairn Lake and Flaco Hernández — whichever copy you use, the book and its contents are the same.
eggs.map_description: Copies sit in three spots: Brian's Marina office (Key Lento, Leonida Keys), the bar at Jacob's Tavern (Millport), and the Taco Bomb in West Kalaga. All three are interiors — in map view you are waypointing the building (marina office, tavern, or Taco Bomb), because the book itself lies on a desk/bar inside and has no map marker of its own.
eggs.confidence: high — multi-source verified (Beebom names the title, author and Flaco plot; Polygon reported the same novel on Nov 20 via GTA6-Life; GameSpot photographed the Jacob's Tavern copy via GTA6Info; SlateSource and RetroBroker list the same book and locations). Whether it proves a shared universe is the outlets' speculation, not a game statement — the book itself is verified.

eggs.name: Arthur Morgan's 'Genuine Cowboy Hat' (Port Gellhorn Yard Sale)
eggs.area: Yard sale in southern Port Gellhorn, Kelly County — driveway northwest of the Dirt Merchants mod shop, off Orchard Avenue
eggs.what_it_is: A wearable replica of Arthur Morgan's rope-banded cowboy hat from Red Dead Redemption 2, sold as a 'Genuine Cowboy Hat' at a balloon-marked yard sale in a residential driveway in Port Gellhorn. It sits on a guitar case resting on a white sofa among the sale items; the seller has no idea what it is. Once bought, it's in your wardrobe permanently and both Jason and Lucia can wear it. PRICE CONFLICT: PC Gamer's original spot and SlateSource/Game8 say $5; Beebom and RetroBroker report $35 (RetroBroker notes reports of $5 near Orchard Avenue or $35 near Calvary Street, possibly two sales or a chapter difference). Budget $35 and be pleasantly surprised if it's $5.
eggs.what_you_get: The Genuine Cowboy Hat — a permanent wardrobe item wearable by both protagonists. Cost: $5 or $35 depending on the sale/report (see what_it_is).
directions: Unlock Lucia / reach Chapter 2 first: Beebom says the hat becomes available after completing 'Discharge Time' and unlocking Lucia in Chapter 2.
Open the map and head to southern Port Gellhorn in Kelly County; find the Dirt Merchants mod shop — Beebom says Orchard Avenue and the nearby Dirt Merchants mod shop will help you locate the sale.
Look northwest of the mod shop, off Orchard Avenue, for yard-sale signs with balloons marking a residential driveway sale.
Find the white sofa/couch in the driveway and the guitar case resting on it among the other items for sale.
Buy the hat on the guitar case, listed in-game as 'Genuine Cowboy Hat' (Beebom lists $35; another report says $5 — the price conflict is noted in this entry's confidence).
Equip it anytime afterward from the wardrobe — both Jason and Lucia can wear it.
eggs.map_description: Southern Port Gellhorn, Kelly County: a balloon-marked driveway yard sale in the small residential neighborhood just northwest of the Dirt Merchants mod shop, near Orchard Avenue (a second price report places a sale near Calvary Street). Waypoint the block northwest of the mod shop rather than the shop itself — the sale is in a driveway off Orchard Avenue, marked on foot by the signs and balloons.
eggs.confidence: medium-high — multi-source verified for the hat, the yard sale and the Port Gellhorn location (PC Gamer's original find, relayed by GTA6-Life; Beebom; Game8; SlateSource; RetroBroker). Confidence is capped by the unresolved $5 vs $35 price conflict between sources, which is stated openly in the entry rather than hidden.

vehicles.name: Gold Pegassi Toros (Casanova Island) — NAMING CONFLICT: see notes
vehicles.real_world_equivalent: Lamborghini Urus (stated by Sportskeeda and video guides)

vehicles.real_world_equivalent: Lamborghini Huracán (Sportskeeda) — CONFLICT: Detonated calls the same gold car a Lamborghini Aventador

vehicles.chapter_available: Parked in free roam; taking it requires the Chapter 3 Key Cloner.
vehicles.confidence: high for location (Sportskeeda + Detonated + WantedKit); security beyond the key cloner is unreported.

vehicles.name: Maibatsu '97 Penumbra FF (Paul Walker Eclipse tribute)
vehicles.real_world_equivalent: 1995 Mitsubishi Eclipse — Brian O'Conner's car from The Fast and the Furious (stated by Polygon, Dexerto, KeenGamer, GTABoom)

Go to the small side door beside the garage and break in — this trips the property alarm, so immediately disable the alarm panel on the wall to your left inside. Open the garage shutter with the interior switch, then get into the green Penumbra FF: smash the window and hotwire, or use the Slim Jim (Chapter 2) for a quieter entry.

NO source found publishes a tracker line for this car, so tracker is 'unknown', not guessed. Best keeper trick (KeenGamer/GTABoom): steal it just before Moses' introductory Chapter 2 mission and make it your FREE first registration. Registration forces a respray that strips the green livery — Polygon/GTABoom note the original paint can be re-bought at Vice Vinyl ($185 paint, $540 with repairs).

vehicles.chapter_available: Stealable as soon as Vice City free roam opens; keepable from Chapter 2 when registration unlocks (Moses).
vehicles.confidence: high — four dedicated guides agree on location, $6,750 registration and the alarm panel; tracker status unreported everywhere.

vehicles.chapter_available: Parked in free roam; taking it needs the Chapter 3 Key Cloner per most guides.
vehicles.confidence: medium — location and car are consistent across many social video guides, but no written guide (Detonated/GTA6GPS/Game8) has documented it or its security yet.

Garage mates per GTABoom: Vitello (advanced tracker, $43,750 register), Itali RSX (advanced, $40,650), Dubsta (standard tracker, $20,750) — all four alarmed + key cloner.

vehicles.chapter_available: Parked in free roam; requires Chapter 3 Key Cloner to take and late-Chapter 3 advanced-tracker service to keep.
vehicles.confidence: high — GTABoom publishes the full scan; Detonated and multiple videos confirm the car and spot.
